text:
alex: FYI customer ACME Payments opened a ticket — their invoice assistant suddenly started returning wrong totals after yesterday's rollout. Customer says tiny prompt tweaks that used to be ignored now flip the parsing logic. link to ticket: https://acme.inc/issue/9876 :frowning:

morgan: ack, can you paste an example prompt that regresses? trying to repro locally quickly.

alex: pasted from the ticket — original working prompt that used to be fine: 
```
SYSTEM: You are InvoiceBot. Extract line items and total in JSON.
USER: Invoice:
- Item: Consulting, Qty: 10, Unit: 150.00
- Item: Hosting, Qty: 1, Unit: 200.00
Return: {items: [{name, qty, unit_price}], total}
```
Customer said changing the hyphen spacing to `-Item:` (no space after hyphen) or adding an extra trailing space before `Return:` now breaks the total calculation. They claim totals go from 1700.00 -> 1550.00 depending on tiny variations.

sara: omg. that's exactly the prompt-template sensitivity class we've seen in a/b canaries before but not this extreme. which model were they on?

alex: they were on `redwood-model-lite-2025` (released in rollout v3.14 last night). Support logs show model hash `rml-2025-quant-v2`.

jake: can you paste the exact failing API call payload? need headers and prompt so we can reproduce tokenization differences.

alex: from customer logs (sanitized): 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-model-lite-2025",
  "input": "SYSTEM: You are InvoiceBot. Extract line items and total in JSON.\nUSER: Invoice:\n-Item: Consulting, Qty: 10, Unit: 150.00\n- Item: Hosting, Qty: 1, Unit: 200.00\nReturn: {items: [{name, qty, unit_price}], total}",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 300
}
```
They said that switching `-Item:` to `- Item:` fixed it.

morgan: thanks. first steps: repro in canary environment with same model hash. if repro, try pinned previous model snapshot (rml-2025-quant-v1) to see if it's a kernel/quant change. I'll spin up test container.

ops-bot: Deploy event: rollout v3.14 completed to 30% of traffic at 2025-11-02T02:12:45Z. Canary group: "invoice-bots" receiving 30%.

alex: customer reported start time 2025-11-02T02:20Z — matches canary window.

sara: if it's only tiny prompt whitespace causing different parse, likely tokenization boundary or reply formatting changed (maybe we changed default tokenizer mapping or a whitespace collapse in our preprocessor). Did we touch prompt normalization in this rollout?

jake: change log: v3.14 included kernel updates and a small preprocessor fix to trim repeated whitespace sequences. commit: 9f3a2b - "normalize contiguous spaces in prompt to single space to reduce prompt length".

morgan: that seems plausible — collapsing multiple spaces could shift token offsets causing model to emit slightly different parsing tokens. But the customer reports a single-space vs no-space after hyphen matters, which is more tokenization than whitespace collapse. we should test both hypotheses.

alex: customer attached model outputs — two examples. Output A (expected):
```json
{
  "items": [
    {"name":"Consulting","qty":10,"unit_price":150.00},
    {"name":"Hosting","qty":1,"unit_price":200.00}
  ],
  "total":1700.00
}
```
Output B (regressed):
```json
{
  "items": [
    {"name":"Consulting","qty":10,"unit_price":150.00} // hosting line dropped due to parsing shift
  ],
  "total":1550.00
}
```

sara: actionable plan: 1) eng-ml reproduce (morgan/jake) 2) if repro, pin fallback for affected customers to previous model snapshot 3) add a quick mitigation: halt the whitespace normalization preprocessor for invoice parsing routes 4) longer-term: add token-boundary sensitive evals to our regression suite.

jake: started local repro with exact payload on rml-2025-quant-v2 — initial result: different JSON ordering but total still 1700. Trying with `-Item:` spacing.

jake: ok repro succeeded when I removed the space after hyphen — model omitted second item. Repro steps: curl with `Content-Type: application/json` and the exact input string above.

jake: diff of tokenization (from local tokenizer tool):
```
Original tokens around hyphen: ["-", "Item", ":"]
No-space tokens: ["-Item", ":"]
```
Token merger leads to different embedding positions which apparently changed the attention pattern for the parsing head.

morgan: good find. can you confirm older snapshot rml-2025-quant-v1 tokenized differently?

jake: checked v1 — it produced ["-","Item",":"] even for `-Item:` due to an older tokenizer normalization rule. so this is a tokenizer change introduced in quant-v2.

sara: that pins cause: tokenizer change in new model artifact + preprocessor whitespace normalization. two small changes multiplied.

alex: what's immediate customer mitigation? they asked for a bandaid — easiest is routing their account to `redwood-model-lite-2025@rml-2025-quant-v1` or an API config to enable legacy tokenization.

morgan: I'll add a temporary customer override to route ACME Payments to the previous snapshot and disable whitespace collapse on invoice routes. I'll also draft a postmortem and customer note.

jake: adding a feature request for a per-customer tokenization flag and default regression tests for token-boundary-sensitive templates.

support-bot: Escalation created: ESC-2025-1123 assigned to eng-ml. SLA: P1 response within 2 hours.

sara: long-term: need automated fuzz tests for our most common templates — invoice, order-confirmation, shipping-label — run them across model variants and tokenizers. This should have been caught by our rollout criteria.

alex: customer asked whether this was a code bug vs model artifact. suggestion: tell them both — apologize, explain we introduced a tokenizer change in a new model snapshot and an incidental preprocessor change that together caused sensitive templates to regress. Offer rollback and whitelist.

morgan: I'll draft the customer message and cc legal if we need credits. Will follow up here when override is in place.

jake: root cause summary (wip): model snapshot `rml-2025-quant-v2` changed tokenization for hyphenated tokens; new preprocessor normalizes space runs. Combined effect changed token boundaries causing parse head to drop second line item for `-Item:` style inputs.

sara: tagging for follow-up: eng-releases for rollout checklist update, eng-ml for tokenizer regression tests, product for customer communication template.

alex: ACME confirmed workaround works when we route them back. closing ticket contingent on postmortem and rollback steps. :white_check_mark:
